form.label: Advanced Workshop #2 — Correlation
form.description: Splunk-side proof that one Collector, two destinations, and one log line carry everything needed to pivot into APM.

div.p: One OpenTelemetry Collector fans data out to two destinations — Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Observability Cloud. A single log line is pivot-able from APM the moment it carries trace_id, service.name, and deployment.environment together — this dashboard proves that correlation holds, and that severity classification actually works, on the Splunk side.

panel.title: % of ALL Log Events Carrying trace_id — Expected to Be Small
panel.description: This is a traffic-mix ratio, not a health signal — do not read a low number here as broken. Only application log lines carry trace_id (via logback); Tomcat access-log lines never do, and access logs vastly outnumber application logs under normal load. The App Log vs Access Log Split panel below shows the same split with both populations labeled. For the metric that DOES have a "good=high" direction, see "% of Application-Layer Logs Carrying trace_id" elsewhere in this row — same field, filtered to just the application-log population.

search.query: index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs | stats count as total, count(eval(isnotnull(trace_id) AND trace_id!="")) as with_trace | eval value=round((with_trace/total)*100,1) | table value
index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs | stats count as total, count(eval(isnotnull(severity))) as classified | eval value=round((classified/total)*100,1) | table value

panel.title: % of Application-Layer Logs Carrying trace_id
panel.description: Same field, different denominator: this filters to application log lines only (identified by the ISO-8601 logback timestamp, excluding Tomcat access-log lines) before computing coverage. Unlike the all-events figure to the left, this one SHOULD read close to 100% — a drop here means the correlation transform itself has stopped working, not that access-log traffic changed shape.

search.query: index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs | eval is_app_log=if(match(_raw,"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T"),1,0) | where is_app_log=1 | stats count as total, count(eval(isnotnull(trace_id) AND trace_id!="")) as with_trace | eval value=round((with_trace/total)*100,1) | table value
index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs trace_id=* severity=* | stats count as value | table value

panel.title: Severity Classification Coverage Over Time — Written at Ingest, Not Retroactive

search.query: index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs | eval s=if(isnull(severity),"UNKNOWN","classified") | timechart span=$span_token$ count by s

panel.title: Single-Event Correlation Proof (Most Recent 15)
panel.description: Each row is one Splunk Enterprise log event that already carries trace_id, service.name, and deployment.environment together. This is exactly what makes the APM service map's "Logs" pivot work: Log Observer Connect (or a manual search) can jump straight from a trace in APM to this event, and back, because the correlating fields already live on the same event — no join, no lookup, no extra pipeline required.

search.query: index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs trace_id=* | rename "service.name" as svc, "deployment.environment" as env | sort -_time | head 15 | table trace_id, severity, svc, env, host

panel.title: Application Log vs Access Log Split (Expected Partial trace_id Coverage)
panel.description: trace_id is auto-extracted only from application log lines that pass through logback. Tomcat access-log lines never carry a trace_id — that is expected and correct, not a bug. This split shows both populations side by side.

search.query: index=k8s_ws_petclinic_logs | eval has_trace=if(isnotnull(trace_id) AND trace_id!="","app log (has trace_id)","access log (no trace_id)") | stats count by has_trace
